          Back on Earth

          • Smoke detectors that ignore dust. A shuttle detector told combustion particles from dust and was used in mines. Our smoke-vs-dust lens shows why: smoke is 0.04–0.3 µm, dust about 1.7 µm. NASA Spinoff
          • Firefighter clothing improved with spacesuit technology. NASA Spinoff
          • Firefighter air tanks made lighter with spacesuit technology. NASA Spinoff
          • Fine-water-mist extinguishers developed for the ISS have uses on Earth (challenge text).
          • Cleaner engines and burners: NASA's own PSI descriptions of FLEX, CFI and SLICE say their cool-flame and flame results inform cleaner, more efficient engines (PSI research-impact text).

          Evidence

          Preview · prints as a clean document (choose "Save as PDF" to keep a file)

          Data

          NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI), combustion investigations, license CC0-1.0. Each run links to its investigation DOI. Some pressures and oxygen values are assumed ISS cabin air where the source table gave none; they are marked and given lower confidence.

          How decisions are made

          Plain arithmetic on the run table, no AI. Evidence strength is a transparency aid, not a safety rating.

          AI use

          The “What the evidence says” panel can show text written by an open AI model; a citation verifier removes any sentence that cites a run outside the evidence, uses a number not in that run, or states a limit or safety verdict. With AI off it shows a fixed template. AI tools also helped the team write documentation and code, and the logo illustration was generated with Google Gemini.
